# Digital ID Hackathon - Southern Africa ### Catalysing growth and prosperity **This hackathon has ended** [Find more hackathons](https://devpost.com/hackathons) [View the winners](https://hackid-southernafrica.devpost.com/project-gallery) ###### Who can participate - Ages 18+ only - College students only - Team required: 2 to 5 members - Only specific countries/territories included [View full rules](https://hackid-southernafrica.devpost.com/rules) [View schedule](https://hackid-southernafrica.devpost.com/details/dates) **Nov 22, 2024 – Feb 9, 2025** | | | | --- | --- | | [Johannesburg, South Africa](https://maps.google.com/?q=Johannesburg%2C%20South%20Africa) | Public | | [**$10,000** in prizes](https://hackid-southernafrica.devpost.com/#prizes) | **101**
participants | [Carnegie Mellon University Africa](https://devpost.com/hackathons?organization=Carnegie+Mellon+University+Africa) [Beginner Friendly](https://devpost.com/hackathons?themes%5B%5D=Beginner+Friendly) [Social Good](https://devpost.com/hackathons?themes%5B%5D=Social+Good) #### **Unleashing the Power of Digital ID in Africa Through Use-cases** **Calling all university students aspiring to be innovators, developers, and policymakers in Southern Africa!** Are you passionate about leveraging technology to drive positive social and economic change? Do you believe digital ID holds the key to unlocking a brighter future for the region? If so, then this hackathon is for you! **Hosted by Carnegie Mellon University Africa’s [Upanzi Network](https://www.africa.engineering.cmu.edu/research/upanzi/index.html) and [Microsave Consulting](https://www.microsave.net/) (MSC), this regional hackathon presents a unique opportunity** to shape the future of digital ID in Southern Africa. The hackathon invites Southern Africa’s next thought leaders to identify and develop high-impact use cases for this transformative technology in various sectors such as healthcare, education, agriculture, access to public services and others. The hackathon is organized under the theme **“Catalysing growth and prosperity”**. ##### **Eligibility criteria** University students from 10 South African countries, (South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini, Mozambique, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Angola and Zambia) can participate in the Southern Africa Digital ID Hackathon by forming a team of 2-5 members. To foster inclusivity, teams must have required at least one active female participant. The refugees and asylum-seekers enrolled in a university in these countries are also eligible to participate. ##### **The hackathon journey** - **Stage 1: Launch & digital ID upskilling (3 weeks):** - We'll kick things off with informative online information sessions to answer all your questions and guide you through the application process. - To equip you with the knowledge and skills necessary for success, we'll be offering a comprehensive free digital ID upskilling course delivered through a series of webinars. - **Stage 2: Idea review & shortlisting (1 week):** - Once the application window closes, our team of experts will review all submitted ideas. - Based on their potential impact, innovation, and feasibility, we'll carefully select 4-5 of the most high-potential use cases to move forward to the next stage. - **Stage 3: Development & refinement (3 weeks):** - Get ready to dive deep into development! We'll provide access to the powerful MOSIP Sandbox, a development environment specifically designed for digital ID solutions. - You won't be alone on this journey. Our team of industry experts will offer invaluable mentorship and support, guiding you through the development process and addressing any challenges you encounter. - To foster collaboration and knowledge sharing, we'll create a dedicated community forum where teams can troubleshoot issues, share insights, and learn from each other. - **Stage 4: Regional award events (2 weeks):** - As you refine your solutions, we'll provide guidance on how to effectively present your use cases to a panel of judges and potential stakeholders. - The culmination of this journey will be the Southern Africa regional award event, which will accommodate both virtual and in-person depending on the participant country of origin. Here, the top teams will have the opportunity to showcase their groundbreaking digital ID solutions in front of a live audience. - The final act will be an award ceremony where we'll recognise and celebrate the most innovative solutions that have the potential to truly transform the way digital ID is used in Southern Africa **But what's in it for you, you ask?** Beyond the immense satisfaction of contributing to a brighter future for the region, you'll gain valuable experience, develop your skills in digital ID and application development, and receive insightful feedback from industry experts. Additionally, the winning team from each region may be invited to a prestigious international platform to showcase their winning solution alongside other leading innovators in the field, marking a significant milestone in their journey. #### Level Up Your Digital ID Skills: Prepare for the Hackathon! **Introducing the Free Digital ID Course:** Developed by Upanzi Network in collaboration with MOSIP and other industry experts, this **self-paced online course** equips you with the fundamentals of Digital ID. Here's what you'll gain: - **Solid understanding of Digital ID:** Grasp the core concepts, benefits, and transformative potential of Digital ID for individuals and society. - **Real-world applications:** Explore inspiring case studies showcasing how Digital ID is already improving lives across Africa. - **MOSIP Platform Proficiency:** Gain technical insights into the [MOSIP platform](https://mosip.io/#1), a foundational platform used by nations to develop Digital ID solutions. **More than just a course, it's your launchpad for success!** ### Requirements #### By completing this course, you'll be well-prepared to brainstorm impactful ideas for the hackathon armed with the knowledge and resources to craft a winning submission. #### Ideation Phase After completing the Digital ID course you'll be well-equipped to tackle the ideation phase of the hackathon. Here's what you need to know to submit your idea: ##### What to Create We have developed a template that will guide you in bringing out the best aspects of your idea. This template must be filled as-is to give your idea the best chance of winning. **Download the Submission Template:**\[ [Find the Template Here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vnfmqdwntCkR83sM7eo3ccbIKj9cUC88x47DisRRPXM/edit?usp=sharing)\] (Fill this out before submitting) **What to submit:** - **Completed submission template as a PDF**: Ensure your completed template is converted into a PDF document.Keep the file size between 10MB and 35MB for easy submission. - **Submission via Devpost**: Head over to the “My Projects” tab, create a project and follow the prompts to upload and submit your completed PDF template. You edit your submission any number of times before the deadline. **Submission deadline:** Don't miss out! All submissions are due by **Sunday, February 9th, 2025 at 11:59 PM UTC.** **Confirmation and support:** By submitting your idea, you confirm that it's your original and unpublished work, and that you've reviewed the official [hackathon rules](https://hackid-africa.devpost.com/rules). Need help with your submission? Join our supportive community on the hackathon's [Discord channel](https://discord.gg/GhYp5AQVbt)! ### Hackathon Sponsors ### Prizes $10,000 in prizes ###### Grand Prize 1 winner \- A laptop for each member of the team \- Business pre-incubation program with CMU-Africa's Industry Innovation Lab \- Fully sponsored chance to attend the ID4Africa 2025 conference in Addis Ababa\* \- A chance to engage in a paid internship with the Upanzi DPG lab\* \\* Please note that some prizes require additional eligibility beyond the control of the organisers and shall be handled at the discretion of the organisers. ###### 1st Runner-up 1 winner \- Business pre-incubation program with CMU-Africa's Industry Innovation Lab \- Sponsor swag & goodies \- Fully sponsored chance to attend the ID4Africa 2025 conference in Addis Ababa\* \\* Please note that some prizes require additional eligibility beyond the control of the organisers and shall be handled at the discretion of the organisers. ### Devpost Achievements Submitting to this hackathon could earn you: ### Judges ![Andrew Musoke](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocJnTm233o8xy8voKDzL9ttL-e_vomz2I2CS1r9vJB5NaFS4Hg=s96-c?type=normal) **Andrew Musoke** _Hackathon Organiser - Upanzi DPI Network_ ### Judging Criteria - **Community Engagement** - **Impact and Community Benefits** - **Overall documentation's accuracy and Clarity** - **Inclusion and Ethical considerations** - **Security and Privacy friendly / Digital rights** - **Relevance to African Context** - **Scalability and Sustainability** - **Feasibility and Practicality** - **Novelty and Creativity** Questions? [Email the hackathon manager](mailto:upanzi@andrew.cmu.edu) **Tell your friends** This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google [Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy) and [Terms of Service](https://policies.google.com/terms) apply. ![]() [Previous image](https://hackid-southernafrica.devpost.com/)[Next image](https://hackid-southernafrica.devpost.com/)

# Build the Future with Entelect Hackathons

Join South Africa’s premier optimisation-first developer competition platform. Compete, iterate, and outperform the best.

Explore Hackathons

![Entelect Hackathons](https://challenge.entelect.co.za/assets/images/home/home_image_1.svg)

#### What is a hackathon?

A hackathon is an event where problem-solvers come together to build solutions within a limited time.

Entelect Hackathons take that concept further. Instead of focusing on building a once-off project, our hackathons centre around optimisation problems. Participants develop solutions that are tested, scored, and ranked based on performance, efficiency, and strategy.

The result is a hackathon experience that feels more like a strategic game — where the best thinkers, not just the fastest builders, come out on top.

![Discovery Gradhack visual](https://www.discovery.co.za/wcm/microsites/gradhack/img/gradhack-main-banner.png)

# At Discovery we are obsessed with doing things differently

## Our business is about changing people’s lives for the better. To be   better for our clients, we are encouraged to always look for new ideas and ways to make those ideas real.

WE’RE ONE OF THE TOP INNOVATORS IN SOUTH AFRICA

Our ambition is to be the best insurance organisation in the world, and a powerful
force for social good. Our company was started by two forward-thinking actuaries, Adrian Gore
and Barry Swartzberg, who are still at the helm of the business. They started an early tradition
in our business of always looking for clever ideas and solutions where others see problems.

Since then, we have become known as innovator and challenger; a business with people
who transform what is ordinary into something extraordinary.

WE HAVE THE DATA. AND THE SPECS!

This year, we will host a virtual Discovery Graduate Hackathon for IT students from South African universities from the 24th - 26th July 2026. 50 students will get a chance to be part of an immersive work experience solving real challenges through technology opportunities in the Discovery environment. The top 3 teams will then be invited to present their ideas to our judging panel at 1 Discovery Place, Sandton on the 7th August 2026. This year the winning team will win R100,000! Participating Gradhackers stand a chance to be permanently employed at Discovery. Please see out FAQ page if you have any questions not answered **[here](https://www.discoverygreen.co.za/assets/microsites/gradhack/gradhack-faqs.pdf)**.

# 50 students will get to experience our exciting environment

Our 2026 Virtual Gradhack runs from 24th to 26th July. Please submit your applications by 31 May 2026 and be one of the students
to take part in this event.

Open to all final year IT and Data Science Students studying at a South African University or Academy.

# Build the Future with Gradhack 2026

Gradhack is Discovery’s annual innovation challenge where top Computer Science and Information Systems and Data Science students collaborate, experiment, and build
technology solutions to real-world problems.

Working in teams, participants design and prototype ideas inspired by real business challenges, using modern tools and technologies — including AI — to bring their solutions
to life.

Selected teams will take part in a fast-paced innovation weekend where creativity, problem-solving, and technical thinking come together.

Every year Gradhack challenges students to solve real-world problems that matter.

For 2026 we’ve identified three opportunity areas where technology — and especially AI — has the potential to create meaningful impact. When submitting your idea, your
team should choose one of the themes below and propose an innovative solution within that space.

If your team is selected for the Gradhack weekend, you will be assigned a new business requirement within the theme you selected, which you’ll use to design and build your
prototype during the event.

![](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/project1.jpg)

### Theme 1 – AI for Personalised Health and Wellness

Technology is transforming the way people manage their health, fitness, and wellbeing.


In this theme we’re interested in ideas that explore how AI could support individuals in building healthier lifestyles, improving performance, and staying motivated over time. Think about how intelligent systems might analyse personal context, respond dynamically to changing conditions, and provide meaningful guidance that helps people achieve their goals.

* * *

###### THE CHALLENGE

We’re looking for solutions that combine data, intelligence, and thoughtful user experience to create truly personalised health journeys.

![](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/project2.jpg)

### Theme 2 – AI for Smarter Everyday Living

Making healthy choices isn’t always easy. Many people struggle with information overload, time constraints, and uncertainty about what choices are best for them.


This theme focuses on how AI and digital innovation could help people make better everyday decisions around food, nutrition, and lifestyle.

* * *

###### THE CHALLENGE

We’re looking for ideas that combine personalisation, behavioural insight, and great product thinking to make healthy living more accessible, engaging, and practical.

![](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/project3.jpg)

### Theme 3 – AI for Safer Communities

Safety and security remain some of the most important concerns for individuals and communities. This theme explores how technology could be used to support safer environments — from individual homes to entire neighbourhoods.
Think about how data, analytics, and intelligent systems might help people act earlier, respond faster, and build stronger community-level protection.

* * *

###### THE CHALLENGE

We’re looking for ideas that show how technology can be used responsibly and creatively to solve meaningful societal challenges.

# **Great Prizes up for grabs**

- **The winning team will receive a cash prize of R100 000**
- **Participating Gradhackers stand a chance to be permanently employed at Discovery**

**Important to note:** Employment offers are subject to candidates having successfully completed their qualification by January 2027.

## Why Gradhack

Gradhack is more than a hackathon. It’s an opportunity to solve meaningful problems, collaborate with talented peers, and experience how real technology teams
work. Participants build working prototypes, engage with Discovery engineers and technology leaders, and demonstrate how they approach real-world challenges.
For many students, Gradhack has been the start of an exciting career journey in technology.

## Launch Your Career

GradHack is also a pathway into a career at Discovery.
Following the event, selected participants will have the opportunity to interview with Discovery business units, where they can showcase their skills and explore
potential roles within the organisation.

Top candidates may be offered **permanent positions,** making GradHack not just an event — but a potential starting point for a career in technology.

## Who Should Apply

Gradhack is designed for curious, creative students who enjoy solving problems and building new ideas. Ideal candidates include final-year students studying:

Computer Science


Information Systems

Software Engineering

Data Science

or related technology disciplines.

We’re looking for students who demonstrate curiosity, structured thinking, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment and learn quickly.

# Submit your idea

## You can enter more than one idea for the same challenge,  or enter more than one challenge.

## Entries to the 2026 Discovery Gradhack are now closed. Be sure to look out for the 2027 event next year.

## A day in the life of a Gradhacker at Discovery

![A day in the life of a Gradhacker at Discovery](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/gradhack-life-1.jpg)

![A day in the life of a Gradhacker at Discovery](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/gradhack-life-2.jpg)

## Meet some of the Discovery IT and Data Science Leaders that you will interact with...

![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/derek.jpg)

## Derek Wilcocks

###### Group CIO

Derek joined Discovery in 2018. He is responsible for Group Information Systems which includes all infrastructure, security, data governance, member and intermediary digital servicing channels, technology innovation and corporate systems. As the chair of the Discovery CIO forum he is also responsible for joint technology initiatives and governance across the Discovery Group worldwide.


![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/nadira.jpg)

## Nadira Naidoo

###### Vitality CIO

Nadira joined Discovery in 2006 as a Business Analyst for the Vitality International Markets. In 2010, she moved over to Vitality RSA and headed up the systems implementation of the projects. Nadira is currently responsible for the IT governance, project delivery, support and finance within the Vitality RSA environment.


![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/kevin.jpg)

## Kevin Dreyer

###### CIO Discovery Insure

Over the last 22 years Kevin has built a distinguished career in Consultancy, Agency, Enterprise environments and Financial Services. He has held various senior leadership roles, including Systems Management and Architecture.


Kevin started his career in 2002 in a very innovative startup and has been involved in startups and scaling businesses ever since. In 2010, he joined Vitality Life, playing a pivotal role in the Discovery Prudential Life journey. He was instrumental in transitioning the business from the PRU JV and defining and implementing a strategy to run the business and systems in both the UK and South Africa, ensuring an exceptional customer experience and delivering on the business strategy. Kevin's leadership helped establish Vitality Life as a leader in Digital, consistently achieving excellent business results.


In the past five years, Kevin has played a critical role in GIS, modernizing platforms, implementing digital transformation, and defining and executing strategies that significantly improve business capabilities. His efforts have significantly enhanced customer and staff experiences, as well as system performance and availability


Kevin's innovative approach and commitment to excellence have been key to the success of the teams that he has led. His unique ability to bridge technical and business domains allows him to effectively communicate with senior business leaders and inspire his team to deliver successful solutions. Kevin continues to demonstrate the Discovery leadership style and remains an inspiring thought leader, driven by his thirst for knowledge and dedication to business success.


![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/angel-robertson.png)

## Angela Robertson

###### Head Of Data Science

Angela joined Discovery a decade ago in the cross-company analytics team, focusing on the application of operations research in the business. The team has grown into the Group Data Science Lab – a team of close to 30 people - which she now leads. Their work follows the theme of _the science of better:_ improving process efficiency, staff productivity, client sentiment and health.

The focus is on the creation of data assets and application of advanced modelling for the local and international markets, using the latest cloud technology. More recent work has seen data science enhance personalisation and precision in the form of new product design and the use of generative AI in servicing.


![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/zaid.jpg)

## Zaid Parak

###### Group Chief Information Security Officer

Zaid has over 20 years of IT experience across a wide range of disciplines, including Networking, Infrastructure, Development, IT Operations, Enterprise Architecture, Security and working knowledge of Risk management with audit exposure.


Zaid joined Discovery in April 2017 and as the Group Chief Information Security Officer, he is accountable for Information Governance and Security at a group level and is responsible for setting the strategy and vision by developing and implementing group-wide programs. He is known for having a bias for action and has laid out a clear strategic path for the information governance security journey in Discovery. He has, since joining, successfully provided distinct strategic and technical leadership for the Information Governance and Security business function across the Discovery Group and knitted together a team under him who are dedicated and focused on preventing and detecting Cyber Crime.


![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/jamieNew.jpg)

## Jamie Whittaker

###### Systems of Engagement CIO

Before joining Discovery, Jamie worked across the EMEA region for Johnson & Johnson. He cut his teeth on any and all projects that came his way during the .com bubble, working as general lackey and web monkey for a number of successful and not so successful dotcoms.


His background is primarily in the design, user champion and web development space. He describes himself as a "part-time thinker, full-time enthusiast, herder of cats" and truly believes that a sense of humour and enthusiasm are the best assets to have on your CV.


![Team Member](https://www.gradhack.co.za/img/johan.png)

## Johan Marais

###### Technology Services Platform Services Manager

## What is the Hackathon?

The Hackathon is a **graduate** coding competition hosted by **Monkey & River** and **Momentum**.

Sign up as an individual, prove yourself through a technical challenge, form a team with other top qualifiers and compete for the chance to **code live at Momentum’s** offices in an 18-hour in-person final.

What programming languages can I use?

Details on the technical challenge will be shared with registered participants. The challenge will involve multiple languages and frameworks.

Do I need to be a student?

You must be a final-year or honours student at a recognised South African institution, or have graduated within the last two years.

What happens at the in-person final?

The top 10 teams compete in an 18-hour coding sprint at Momentum’s offices in Centurion. You’ll code overnight, present your solution to a panel of judges, and winners are announced on day two.

Is there a cost to enter?

No. The hackathon is free to enter.

Will food be provided at the final?

Yes. Dinner, breakfast, lunch, snacks, and beverages are provided for all finalists across both days.

pageTitle: GirlCode | Hackathon
title: GirlCode Hack 2024
description: An annual 30-hour hackathon celebrating women's month in South Africa, aimed at enhancing coding skills among young women in university/college, promoting female technical talent, and driving positive change in line with UN SDGs.
eligibility: Open to young women in university/college
themes: Harness the power of technology to address pressing global challenges outlined in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
prizes: Overall winning team will win a cash prize valued at R100,000 and will participate in a 6-month accelerator program. Prize tiers for teams in each participating country include laptops, tablets, headphones, a power bank, and motivational books.
teamRequirements: Teams should consist of young women; specific team size not stated.
rawMarkdown:
GirlCodeHack is an annual 30 hour hackathon held in August, in celebration of Women’s month in South Africa.This year's hackathon is a special one, as GirlCode is Celebrating 10 Years and this hackathon will span over 10 African cities.

The hackathon is designed to spark, renew and elevate an interest in coding amongst young women, in particular those that are in University/College. The hackathon was created to provide young women, eager to join the software industry with an opportunity to develop some of the real-world skills they need to enter the world of work. Through the hackathon, we aim to raise awareness of female technical talent and foster a competitive, yet cooperative, and congenial culture for talented female techie.

The overarching theme of the GirlCode Hackathon revolves around aligning technology, innovation, and female empowerment to drive positive change within the context of the UN SDGs. Each participating team will delve into one specific goal, exploring creative and impactful solutions that not only address the challenges presented but also contribute to the sustainable development of their communities and beyond.

## 2024 Hackathon

Join us for this incredible annual event where talented women in tech converge to build groundbreaking solutions and make their mark in the tech world!

👩‍💻Theme: **Harness the power of technology to address pressing global challenges outlined in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**

Preview

About AI MashUp

The AI Mashup is more than just an artificial intelligence-themed Hackathon. It is a combination of virtual and in person events, hosted simultaneously in multiple locations. This year we are starting with multiple provincial locations across South Africa and have plans to expand into other Sub Saharan African countries next year.

The AI Mashup offers virtual and in-person activities, skills training, and post-event support. Participants are encouraged to leverage AI capabilities to create unique solutions for provided challenge statements or demonstrate enhanced functionality to existing solutions through the use of AI.

Partners and participants who dare to approach challenges differently are encouraged to register.

![](data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,%3Csvg height='120.00000000000001' width='321' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' version='1.1'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

![](https://mlab.co.za/static/8a948a02b9d7d16a9ff618d6f7beb9cd/0e446/techBlob.png)

The Mashup

The AI Mashup will be hosted under the theme of Sustainable Artificial Intelligence.

It will focus on teams that can develop solutions under the following themes, which have been identified as having a significant impact on the social and economic landscape of Africa:

- Fintech

- Healthtech

- Edutech

- Agritech


![](data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,%3Csvg height='120.00000000000001' width='321' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' version='1.1'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

![](https://mlab.co.za/static/8a948a02b9d7d16a9ff618d6f7beb9cd/0e446/techBlob.png)

Apply to participate

Participants get to increase their AI knowledge as well as build and showcase an AI solution to industry leaders. In addition, winning teams will receive cash prizes as well as post-event support opportunities. Participants will also receive:

- Mentors

- Meals & drinks

- Toiletry bags

- Corporate gifts


![](data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,%3Csvg height='120.00000000000001' width='321' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' version='1.1'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

![](https://mlab.co.za/static/8a948a02b9d7d16a9ff618d6f7beb9cd/0e446/techBlob.png)

Become a Partner

Register to be part of our partner briefing session - where you will find out more about the Partnership Packages and available benefits for your organisation. The AI Mashup is a combination of specific ecosystem building activities that are designed to address local challenges, foster innovation, and nurture local talent. Partner with us to:

- Share thought leadership

- Crowdsource solutions & data insights

- Identify tech talent

- Make an impact

## Problem Statements:

The problem statements below cover a range of societal challenges and opportunities, aligning with various domains where innovative app solutions can make a significant impact. Participants in the hackathon can choose the problem statement that resonates with them and develop creative, impactful app solutions.

Click on a problem statement to find out more details

Access to higher education

### Access to higher education

×

#### **Problem statement**

How might technology help young South Africans find suitable study pathways, compare funding options, complete applications and remain supported from acceptance through graduation?

#### Possible focus areas

Applications, bursaries and NSFAS guidance; cost planning; student wellness; academic persistence; connectivity and accessible learning.

Close

Youth employment and work readiness

### Youth employment and work readiness

×

#### Problem statement

How might we shorten the distance between young people and meaningful income by translating skills into credible profiles, practical experience, work opportunities and career mobility?

#### Possible focus areas

Skills verification; entry-level matching; micro-internships; mentorship; informal experience; transport and data barriers.

Close

Youth entrepreneurship and small-business growth

### Youth entrepreneurship and small-business growth

×

#### Problem statement

How might digital tools help young founders and township or rural businesses start, trade, get paid, manage cash flow and reach formal markets?

#### Possible focus areas

Business registration; digital payments; bookkeeping; procurement access; market links; funding readiness and fraud protection.

Close

Financial inclusion and money confidence

### Financial inclusion and money confidence

×

#### Problem statement

How might we make everyday money management simpler, safer and more useful for people with irregular incomes, limited financial knowledge or limited access to formal services?

#### Possible focus areas

Budgeting; saving; responsible credit; low-data tools; multilingual support; scam awareness; accessible design.

Close

Safer communities and gender-based violence response

### Safer communities and gender-based violence response

×

#### Problem statement

How might technology help people find trusted support, document incidents safely, access emergency help and strengthen prevention without placing survivors at greater risk?

#### Possible focus areas

Privacy-first reporting; verified services; discreet access; referral pathways; community education; responsible data governance.

Close

Climate resilience and essential services

### Climate resilience and essential services

×

#### Problem statement

# Schools, hackathons and Skills Development

IDIA supports data science hackathons, research schools and skills-development events through ilifu access, logistical support and tailored data challenges.

## Accelerated learning with hackathons

Between 2020 and mid-2026, IDIA helped deliver 33 successful hackathons by providing ilifu access, logistical support and data science challenges based on real research problems across astronomy, food science, public health and other fields. This was done in collaboration with a diverse group of partners, including the DSTI, the Office of Astronomy for Development (OAD), DARA Big Data, the African Astronomical Society (AfAS), the BRICS Astronomy BITDN project, and the IAU General Assembly 2024.

## The Future of Hackathons

![Hack4Dev logo](https://www.idia.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/TRAIN_Hack4DevLogo.png)

In May 2022, Associate Professor Carolina Odman-Govender established Hack4dev to unite partners around a broader hackathon vision. IDIA helped develop a structured, cascade-based hackathon framework to strengthen the long-term impact of these events. First implemented in July 2024, the programme trains regional organisers and supports a growing network of data science hackathons across Africa.

The first Data Science Trainers Hackathon was held at Wits University in October 2024, with a second regional series planned for 2026/2027.

[Hack4Dev Website](https://hack4dev.org/)

![Map graphic for future hackathon programme](https://www.idia.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/TRAIN_banner_map_option1.jpg)

## Research Schools

At research schools, students receive lectures from leaders in big data in science and industry, then form teams to tackle data-intensive projects. The projects run on the IDIA Research Cloud with substantial computational and storage resources allocated for the event.

# Hackathons, Bootcamps & Idea Competitions: Driving Impact

With support from our partners and donors, we have had the pleasure of hosting an annual hackathon since 2023 and hosted our first Idea Competition in 2024

[Innovation Pillar](https://financialinnovationhub.org.za/innovation) [Learn Who We Are](https://financialinnovationhub.org.za/about-us)

# 2026

## UCT-Cortex Hub FinTech Lab Inaugural Summer School and Hackathon

### Sponsored by the FirstRand Foundation

**Growing in more directions.** From the 12th of January to the 30th of January, the Financial Innovation Hub in collaboration with The Cortex Hub kicked-off the UCT-Cortex Hub FinTech Lab with our inaugural FinTech Summer School Programme in East London, Eastern Cape. The FinTech Lab is sponsored by the FirstRand Foundation.

The Summer School programme included a two week bootcamp where the first week was on Open Banking and the second week on Technical Development where participants were taught full stack development and exposed to specialised topics such as mobile application development, Blockchain and Data Science. The final week culminated in a 5 day hackathon where teams were expected to produce a working POC applying a open banking via a Hub-built Open Banking sandbox with simulated data, a business plan on their idea and a pitch deck. The hackathon theme:

Teams were required to present in a mock pitch to an industry panel, this time the Investment Committee of Convergence Partners, global private equity firm based in South Africa, giving valuable feedback before their final pitch the next day. The final pitch were judged by representatives of Cortex Hub and the Financial Innovation Hub. Made up of the Chair of the Cortex Hub board, Nico Muka, Lunga Feni, Partnerships lead at the Cortex Hub, Dr Allan Davids, Director of the Financial Innovation Hub, And Takunda Chirema, Senior Software Engineer at the Financial Innovation Hub, Nobulali Myataza, ESD Specialist at the Cortex Hub and Anda Ngcaba, Innovation Director of the Financial Innovation Hub.

Prizes include Takealot vouchers of amounts R5000, R2500 and R1000 for split equally amongst first, second and third teams. Top placing teams are eligible to apply to the GenesisBloc Launchpad pre-incubator with their hackathon idea for the Financial Inclusion Stream.

‍

Our first programme acted as a pilot, accepting 21 undergraduates or alumni of Walter Sisulu University, University of Fort Hare, Nelson Mandela University and Rhodes as well as Cortex Hub entrepreneurs. We hope to grow this number to reach more talented inviduals in the eastern cape in our Next winter school edition of the programme, in June 2026.

# 2025

## Financial Innovation Hub x Interledger Bootcamp and Hackathon

### Financial Innovation Hub x Interledger 2025

Back bigger and better! This year's week-long event welcome students from across the entire UCT community, from first-year undergraduates to postdoctoral researchers. The 4-day Bootcamp, held in June 2025, featured sessions led by Allan Davids (Senior Lecturer at UCT), Sabine Schaller (Lead Engineer at Interledger), and Takunda Chirema (Technical Specialist at Hub). The program covered topics such as payments, full-stack development, and the Interledger Protocol, offering both practical and theory-based content.

The event concluded with a hackathon on the 5th and 6th days, where this year around 100 participants formed 16 student teams to bootstrap a proof of concept and pitch their startup idea to a panel of industry judges. Teams competed for a prize pool of R65,000 sponsored by the Interledger Foundation.

A special shoutout to the Interledger Foundation as always for bringing to Cape Town their whole team of senior developers, product designers and product leads who volunteered their expertise throughout the full 7-day event.

## Algorand Workshops and Hackathon

### Financial Innovation Hub Algorand Developer Workshop Series 2023

Led by Gary Lu, these Algorand Developer Workshops were held in April, 2023 for six sessions over two weeks in both online and in-person formats. These were entry-level, highly-practical sessions where the aim is to bootstrap potential hackathon participants and beginners looking to get coding on the Algorand blockchain.

Links to the slides used in each session are included each video. See this [GitHub repository](https://github.com/FinHubSA/AlgorandDevWorkshop) for instructions on how to access the practical components of the workshops. Participants were expected to code along to complete the smart contracts with the workshop lead in GitLab.

We hold at least one hackathon annually with our donors or external partners generally in conjunction with a workshop series focusing on the specific technology. On 28 March 2026, Entelect is once again partnering with the Institute of Information Technology Professionals South Africa (IITPSA) to host an exciting one-day hackathon. Featuring a prize pool of R20,000, the event will bring together some of the brightest talents in the tech industry.

This collaboration underscores Entelect and IITPSA’s shared commitment to driving innovation and excellence in South Africa’s ICT sector.

Participants will have the opportunity to showcase their technical prowess and network with industry professionals and like-minded individuals. Entelect not only designs the problem statement for the hackathon but hosts the event too. Participants can register on the Entelect Challenge website here:

[https://challenge.entelect.co.za](https://challenge.entelect.co.za/)

Registration is open until the start of the of the event. This hackathon is only open to all IITPSA members.

The virtual hackathon will take place on Discord from 10:00 to 15:00 on 28 March 2026.

The StepOne AI Buildathon is a national-level online hackathon designed to identify exceptional builders who can create real-world AI systems for marketing automation.

Participants will develop an intelligent content engine that transforms raw event media into platform-ready marketing assets without human intervention.

The StepOne AI Buildathon is not a traditional coding competition. It is a search for builders who can design systems that solve real business problems with clarity, robustness, and intelligence. StepOne, an experiential marketing company, executes large-scale brand events across India. Each event generates hundreds of photos and videos, which are currently processed manually into marketing assets.

This hackathon challenges participants to automate that entire workflow using AI. Participants will build a Content Intelligence Engine that takes raw event media as input and produces publish-ready outputs for multiple platforms including LinkedIn, Instagram posts, Instagram stories, and a structured case study draft. The system must not only generate high-quality outputs but also define its own selection logic for choosing the best assets. The challenge is designed to test not just output quality, but also system thinking.

Teams must ensure their solution works consistently across different datasets without manual intervention. In addition, they are required to clearly document their architecture, decision-making process, and system limitations. The hackathon will be conducted fully online.

Teams will submit their final working prototypes along with supporting documentation and walkthrough videos. From all submissions, the top 10 teams will be shortlisted based on evaluation criteria such as output quality, platform differentiation, robustness, and clarity of architecture.

These top 10 teams will then be invited for a final pitching round where they will present their systems and thinking in depth. Beyond prize money, this hackathon serves as a hiring funnel for StepOne, with select participants being offered the opportunity to work on building the company’s AI-powered marketing platform. This is an opportunity to build something meaningful, solve a real-world problem, and potentially become part of a product that redefines how marketing is executed.

The Netweb AI for Public Good Hackathon - Ideatron is structured to maximize learning, creativity, and real-world impact. This comprehensive plan covers the event flow, provide students, and startups with inspiring yet feasible project ideas, and ensures they have the data and tools needed. The evaluation criteria tie directly to the goals, promoting solutions that are not just technically sound, but truly beneficial to society. By the end of the event, we expect a range of prototypes tackling important issues – from healthcare and education to environment and governance – demonstrating how local talent can apply AI to create a positive change. The top teams, as identified through our rigorous but fair scoring system, will earn their reward and perhaps even get a chance to implement these solutions in the real world.

Overall, this hackathon initiative will showcase technology’s power in addressing social challenges and hopefully motivate all participants to continue pursuing “AI for Public Good” even beyond the competition, embodying the principle that technology coupled with empathy and innovation can drive meaningful progress in our communities.

Netweb proposes to host a 2-day hackathon (8 hours each day) focused on “AI for Public Good” in the local context of India. The event will bring together 8 teams (2-3 students each) to develop innovative AI-driven solutions that address pressing social and environmental challenges. The primary objectives are:

● Harness AI for Public Impact: Encourage students to apply artificial intelligence techniques to solve real-world problems in areas like healthcare, agriculture, education, environment, public welfare, etc., with a focus on India’s needs. Solutions should demonstrate clear social benefits and align with responsible AI practices.

● Faster Innovation and Learning: Provide an environment for creative thinking, collaboration, and rapid prototyping. Students will receive orientation and mentoring to help translate ideas into prototypes using open data and open-source tools.

● Promote Open Data and open Source: Emphasize use of freely available datasets (e.g., government open data portals) and open-source software/platforms to ensure accessibility and reproducibility of solutions. Participants will be introduced to various open data repositories and AI development platforms during the event.

● Talent Recognition: Identify top talent for potential recruitment. The hackathon will culminate in project evaluations and a leaderboard. The top 3 teams (based purely on evaluation scores) will earn opportunities to possible showcase their prototypes at Netweb future events, incentivizing quality outcomes, along with goodies, prizes and certificate of participation.

  • Contributor: individuals with passion for contributing to the multiple projects during the season and improving the projects with new ideas or solve the existing bugs, etc.

  • Mentor: Professionals with knowledge and experience that can help contributors in the right direction during the contribution period of 2 months.

The Hackathon is structured in two stages: An Online Preliminary Round and an Offline Final round. In the online preliminary round, participants are required to create a presentation that explains the architecture of their projects. This presentation should include elements including, but not limited to, flowcharts and high-level system diagrams, details about the tech-stack used, and a peek into how Intel Developer Cloud is supposed to be integrated into the project's framework.

Round 1: Online Submission Round

In this online qualifying round, participants must submit a comprehensive presentation to showcase their project effectively.

Maintain professionalism, adhere to guidelines.

Note: Participants are required to use Intel Developer Cloud, irrespective of the chosen track. Projects incorporating the Intel oneAPI Developer toolkit will receive preference in the final evaluation, further highlighting the significance of Intel's technologies in this competition.

The Presentation must follow the guidelines mentioned below:

1. Title and Team Introduction:

● A compelling title that encapsulates the essence of your project.

● Mention LinkedIn and GitHub IDs of your team members.

2. Project Overview:

● Present a concise and precise overview of your project's objectives and goals.

● Spotlight the salient features and functionalities that your project delivers.

3. Architectural Insight:

● Comprehensive flowcharts or system diagrams illustrating the key components and their interactions.

● A clear depiction of the data flow within the system.

4. Interface(overview):

● Display the user interface design, including screenshots or mock-ups of key screens.

● Explain how the design choices align with the project's goals and objectives.

5. Intel Developer Cloud Integration(Mandatory):

● Explain your utilisation of the Intel Developer Cloud and oneAPI toolkits(use of toolkits is optional).

6. Application:

● Future scope and elaborate the application of your project in real-world and financial potential.

It is imperative that your presentation remains polished, coherent, and visually engaging. Utilize visual aids such as diagrams, charts, and relevant screenshots to enhance comprehension.

Round 2: Offline Project Showcase Round

The Top 25 teams from the first round will be shortlisted and invited to bring their submitted ideas to life by creating projects, and it's mandatory that they utilize the Intel Developer Cloud, as specified in the previous round. The teams will showcase their projects offline in front of our esteemed panel of judges at GGSIPU EDC. Further details will be communicated to the qualifying teams. Good luck with your projects!

Above all, ensure that your presentation effectively conveys the inventive and impactful nature of your project, all within the framework and guidelines set forth for the hackathon

Power plants are the biggest consumers of coal. Typically a 1000 MW plant consumes about 5 million tonnes of coal annually. India's total coal-based power generation capacity is about 2 lakh MW, which theoretically can consume approximately 1000 million tonnes of coal annually.

Even 10% of that, if replaced with torrefied charcoal will amount to 100 million tonnes of this fuel which will require approximately 165 MTPA of agro residue (considering 60% yield), sufficient to wipe out the entire unused agro residue in the country and thus eliminating the farm fires and produce approx. 20,000 MW of renewable power. The idea has vast potential to increase rural income, provide local employment, cleaning the air by eliminating farm fires and also to generate enormous renewable energy with existing coal power infrastructure.

The technology to produce torrefied fuel using agro residue biomass is not easily accessible to small entrepreneurs due to the higher cost of imported machines, lack of sufficient manufacturers, and non-availability of the torrefaction plants having smaller capacity suitable for cottage industry entrepreneurs. To fast-track the development the technology for converting agro residue to charcoals, NVVN, a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC limited, in partnership with EESL plans to organise a technology challenge Green Charcoal Hackathon. It will leverage the innovative Indian mind to bridge the technology gap, with the prime objective to clean the air by eliminating farm fire, producing renewable energy out of the agro residue, to promote local entrepreneurship, and to increase the income of the farmers.

Nearly half a million road accidents happen every year in India and over hundred and fifty thousand people die every year. Those numbers are comparable to some of the most major natural disasters or even epidemics. Yet road safety elicits less attention that it should. The brightest minds of our generation are making mobility awesome by working on electric vehicles but the other part of making mobility awesome is to end the needless physical harm on our roads.

How can we make our roads safer ? 

There are many ways of making our roads safer: prevention and mitigations. Prevention is where we prevent an accident, mitigation is where we do better handling of accidents. Both can make a difference to overall lives lost on roads. Within prevention :

We can make roads safer by making safer infrastructure (better light conditions, signage, roads etc.). Let’s call them ‘Where we drive’ factors.  

At another level we can make roads safer by making our vehicles safer - we could call them ‘What we drive’ factors

And lastly we could just drive well - the ‘how we drive’ factors.

Goes without saying that if we could improve the ‘how we drive’ - we can achieve safety at the least cost and at an individual level. ‘Where we drive’ & ‘What we drive’ is a much larger canvas of problem solving and needs many stakeholders to make a dent in the problem but ‘How we drive’ interventions can be driven faster. So we want to focus on them for this hackathon.

So how do we solve the problem of making our driving safer - how do we help people drive safer through awareness, through incentives, through gamification, how do we make sure that people are driving safely to start with. That would mean that they are driving within speed limits, not overtaking unnecessarily, braking slowly - so others can adjust, accelerate gently so others can figure out, keeping enough distance between their vehicles and so on.

For example: experts say that nearly a quarter of accidents happen because of distracted driving - with mobile usage a major part of the problem. So how do we stop people from using their mobile phones while driving ?

A hackathon is a time-bound event where participants collaborate to build innovative projects, prototypes, or solutions to real-world problems. Teams typically have 24-72 hours to ideate, develop, and present their solutions. Most hackathons on Reskilll are online, allowing you to participate from anywhere in India. ### Are these hackathons free to join? Yes, most hackathons listed on Reskilll are completely free to participate in. Some premium or corporate hackathons may have a small registration fee, but this is clearly mentioned on the hackathon page. We believe innovation should be accessible to everyone. ### Can beginners participate in hackathons? Absolutely! Many hackathons on our platform are beginner-friendly and welcome students with all skill levels. Hackathons are one of the best ways to learn by doing. You'll get mentorship, collaborate with teams, and build real projects. Look for hackathons tagged as "beginner-friendly" or those that provide starter templates. ### How do I form a team for a hackathon? After registering for a hackathon on Reskilll, you can either create your own team and invite members, or join an existing team. Many hackathons also have a team formation phase where solo participants can connect with others. Team sizes typically range from 2-5 members. ### What can I win in a hackathon? # Learn AI skills through the SAS Hackathon

26 August 20255 Mins Read

[![Advance your career with hands on AI experience through the SAS Hackathon](https://iafrica.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Advance-your-career-with-hands-on-AI-experience-through-the-SAS-Hackathon-scaled.jpg.webp)](https://iafrica.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Advance-your-career-with-hands-on-AI-experience-through-the-SAS-Hackathon-scaled.jpg "Learn AI skills through the SAS Hackathon")

Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how we work. As more organisations explore and adopt agentic, generative, traditional and even quantum AI, these technologies increasingly augment existing jobs. And they automate repetitive and data-driven tasks. More than ever, people need data and AI skills to boost their productivity and further their careers.

That’s where the SAS Hackathon can help. The fifth annual [**SAS Hackathon**](https://www.sas.com/hackathon), open for registration through 31 August 2025, provides real-word experience that can expand critical and in-demand AI skills.

The SAS Hackathon is for people of all job roles and levels of experience, from data scientists, IT developers and business analysts to executives, consultants and students.

The SAS Hackathon is a global, month long, all-digital event. Teams of participants collaborate and compete to solve business and social challenges using the latest AI and advanced analytics.

**Use the latest AI tech**

To participate in the actual hacking, which runs 15 September through 10 October 2025, SAS Hackathon teams must select a challenge, identify data to analyse, and register on the SAS Hackathon site by 31 August 2025.

Approved teams will then have access to the latest AI and advanced analytics, including [**SAS® Viya®**](https://www.sas.com/en_za/software/viya.html), SAS’ cloud-native and cloud-agnostic data and AI platform; [**SAS Viya Workbench**](https://www.sas.com/en_za/software/viya/workbench.html), a cloud-based developer environment for building AI models; and [**SAS Data Maker**](https://www.sas.com/en_za/software/data-maker.html), a secure synthetic data generator.

“AI is transformational, but how do you cut through the hype and build relevant, real-world AI skills? Enter the SAS Hackathon,” said Einar Halvorsen, Global Hackathon Producer at SAS. “The hands-on experience and AI contacts you’ll gain will help advance your career, whether you are an established data or business professional or a student just starting out.”

**AI in action**

In the most recent SAS Hackathon, teams addressed a host of challenges, including:

·         **Worker safety** – used AI and synthetic data technology to develop an AI-enabled heat stroke prevention system for construction workers.

·         **Manufacturing quality** – applied computer vision and machine learning to create an automated system for inspecting injectable pharmaceuticals, improving quality and ensuring product safety.

·         **Improving decision making** – built a tool to verify and assess data sources, spot unreliable information and ensure the use of ethical information to make decisions.

·         **Nuclear site selection** – assessed natural hazard risks in the site selection of nuclear power plants, using AI and machine learning.

·         **Better patient care** – created a system that delivers engaging and safe rehabilitation for stroke patients.

·         **Saving time and money for banks** – automated the extraction of business rules from policy documents and resolved gaps in credit policies.

·         **Evaluating apparel supply chains** – developed a machine learning system that grades factory compliance with established labour standards.

·         **Optimising water management** – created comprehensive climate visualisations of the Dutch river delta.

·         **Reducing billing errors** – built a solution to automate line-by-line auditing of medical bills, reducing errors and preventing losses.

A panel of AI and analytics experts will judge all SAS Hackathon entries, and category and industry winners will be announced this fall.

**Industry tracks**

Teams from an organisation or made up of individuals can join the SAS Hackathon in several industry categories. Industry tracks for this year’s SAS Hackathon include banking; energy and telecom; health care and life sciences; insurance; public sector; retail, consumer goods and manufacturing; and Internet of Things (IoT, a cross-industry track).

**New student track**

While students can create or join teams in the industry tracks, this year’s SAS Hackathon offers a new option, Students can register for the Student Individual track using their academic email. Participants in this track will use Cortex, an analytics simulation game developed by SAS with HEC Montréal, Canada’s first business school, to tackle a fundraising challenge.

SAS, a leader in data and AI, produces the annual SAS Hackathon, which is sponsored by Microsoft and Intel.

# Resources

Annual Trade Event & Conference

## AI Expo Africa 2026 (JHB)

- [Visit Website](https://aiexpoafrica.com/%20)

AI Expo Africa is the official annual gathering of the association and is the largest B2B trade show and conference focused on Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Automation & Smart Technologies in Africa. Attended by 3400+ delegates and with a wider community reach of 50K+ local and regional AI practitioners, AI Expo Africa is now entering its 9th successful year.  The event is attended by Enterprise buyers, Governments, decision makers, international trade missions, vendors, SMBs and global brands all focused on real world business applications you can deploy TODAY.  Its a great place to find new clients, channel partners, learn about local trends and find new markets. **Learn more** >\> [aiexpoafrica.com](https://aiexpoafrica.com/)

Government & Citizen AI Event & Dialogue

## Activate SA 2026 (CPT)

- [Visit Website](https://activatesa.ai/)

Activate South Africa 2026 is the nation’s first government and society centric event dedicated to Responsible AI. This landmark forum explores how South Africa can harness AI to improve service delivery, education, and the everyday lives of its citizens, while establishing the policies, infrastructure, investments and frameworks needed for ethical AI adoption and economic growth.

Convened by the SA AI Association, the creators of Africa’s largest AI ecosystem, Activate SA runs for 2 days in Cape Town and is focused on 10 core topics addressing the challenges and opportunities required to make Responsible AI accessible to all. Executive focused networking, 4x master class CPD 200 seat workshops & AI Startup / Investor showcase make this an event not to be missed if you are seeking access to decision makers and regional influence.

**Learn more** >\> [activatesa.ai](https://www.activatesa.ai/)

![Activate South Africa 2026](https://saaiassociation.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ActivateSA.webp)

![Western Cape AI Cluster](https://saaiassociation.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Western-Cape-AI-Cluster_img.png)

Strategic Collaboration

## Western Cape AI Cluster

In March 2026 the South African AI Association (SAAIA) & the Western Cape Government (WCG) launched the Western Cape AI Cluster (WCAIC).

WCAIC is a 3-year collaborative, multi-stakeholder programme to place the Western Cape as a globally significant AI Tech Hub and gateway to AI Africa.

WCAIC will research, support and grow the artificial intelligence opportunity in the province by engaging relevant stakeholders on key themes such as AI Policy, Responsible AI, Governance, Infrastructure, AI Factories and Sovereign AI.

The WCAIC annual event, Activate SA, convenes every August in Cape Town to share progress within the WC AI Cluster through dialogue, panels, networking, workshops and AI startup / Investor showcase.

**Join WCAIC here** >\> [WCAIC Joining Form](https://forms.gle/dXNy5WfteiQHxuGT9)

## Ready 4 AI Assessment Tool

Is your company Ready 4 AI?  Are you considering, adopting or building AI and automation solutions in your organization?  Confused on where to start or feeling overwhelmed? Had a pilot project fail or just wanting some expert advice?  If the answer is “yes” the SA AI Association can help connect you to our knowledge base, training offerings, deployment consultants and specialist vendors to ensure you achieve your desired goals and ensure success.  We work with all sizes of company in both commercial, government and NGO sectors, startups, mid-size or large enterprises.

- [Learn more & download it here](https://saaiassociation.co.za/ready-4-ai/)

## State of AI in Africa Report

- [Visit Website](https://aiafricareport.gumroad.com/)

The State of AI in Africa Report offers an analysis of the emerging Artificial Intelligence (AI) landscape in Africa. It contains multiple statistics and trends while offering insights into key communities driving the ecosystem across the continent. This report will appeal to analysts, enterprises, channel managers, governments, VCs / investors, NGOs, Embassies, trade missions & regional promotion agencies who are seeking deeper insights about the dynamics of this rapidly growing frontier tech market.

**Download it here** >\> [AI Media Research Reports](https://aiafricareport.gumroad.com/)

Trade Journal & Magazine

## Synapse Magazine

Synapse Magazine chronicles the 4th Industrial Revolution as it unfolds in Africa and plays a vital part in connecting the members of this rapidly growing trade community across the region. With a global readership, it puts Africa centre stage with a clear focus on the African 4IR innovation & investment narrative. We cover a range of technologies including; artificial intelligence (AI), intelligent automation (IA), robotic process automation (RPA), internet of things (IoT), big data, analytics & devices, as well as emerging standards, ethics and privacy concerns.

**Read it here** >\> [issuu.com/aimediasynapse](https://issuu.com/aimediasynapse)

- [Visit Website](https://issuu.com/aimediasynapse)

## AI TV

[AI TV](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC0MFKu_a5_kRqcR4D1rmaxQ?view_as=subscriber) is a streaming channel that forms part of our wider vision to create an AI Powered Future for Africa.  Our goal is to inform people about what to expect as we embrace the fourth industrial revolution in Africa for social and economic benefit. We interview 4IR thought leaders and innovators driving AI & Data Science across the region, including; large companies, SMMEs, innovators, investors and community builders.  We are focused on telling African good news stories about the growing interest in artificial intelligence in the Africa region. ## What is a Hackathon?

A Hackathon is a competition where you try to solve real problems by building a prototype **in 24 or 48 hours**. In Hackathons, which are mostly entered as a team, you can improve yourself with mentoring, **present in front of experienced jury members and compete for the prize!**

## What is a Datathon?

In Datathons — also called Data Marathons or Machine Learning Challenges — you can build the best prediction model **by working on real-life datasets**. In competitions that usually last 2 weeks, you can compete with data, **improve yourself in jury presentations and compete for the prize!**

![](https://coderspace-storage-prod.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/static/img/v3/events/intro-hackathon.webp)

## Why should you join a Hackathon?

Code, build, show your creativity. Solve real problems, win prizes and meet new people along the way.

### Build solutions to real problems

The best way to learn is to practice... Develop yourself by challenging Million Dollar problems!

### Compete for big prizes

Improve yourself while coding in a short time, gain different perspectives from experienced mentors and compete with your team for grand prizes!

### Code with your own team

You don't always get the opportunity to work with your friends. Develop with the team you are most comfortable with for 48 hours!

What is a Hackathon?

A Hackathon is a competition where you try to solve real problems by developing prototypes in 24 or 48 hours. In Hackathons, which are mostly entered as a team, you can improve yourself with mentoring, present in front of experienced jury members and compete for the prize!

Hackathons are competitions where designers, developers, engineers, game developers and technology enthusiasts come together to build prototypes within a limited time.

Now is the time to join a Hackathon! The great competitions we host are waiting for you. Browse the Hackathons, find the one that suits you and start competing!

Why should you join a Hackathon?

Hackathons have many benefits:

###### Networking

Hackathons are quite popular in Turkey. Many experts in their field take part in them. You share the same interests as the other people who join a Hackathon, which means you can learn something from them. You also get the chance to connect and get in touch with the employees of the partner company and with other participants.

###### Collaboration

Having the chance to work with like-minded people and share knowledge puts you in a better position. Hackathons also help you develop your teamwork skills.

###### Innovation

The purpose of a Hackathon is to generate new ideas and build prototypes. So every Hackathon is where innovation is born. Hackathons are a perfect opportunity to brainstorm and come up with solutions — even to global problems. They are events that boost inspiration, innovation, creativity and productivity.

###### Time Management

Because Hackathons ask you to build the expected project within a limited time, they help you improve your time management skills. In a Hackathon you compete both against your rivals and against yourself. Hackathons are one of the best ways to develop the skills of following a plan, staying on target and managing your time well.

###### Learning Opportunity

You learn great new things while working on projects. Working alongside other experts turns a Hackathon into a valuable learning experience.

###### Career Opportunity

By joining Hackathons you can expand your professional network, and if you perform well you can even land a new job opportunity. Listing the Hackathons you joined on your resume also helps you prove your skills to employers.

Compete in Hackathons

- Apply on your own or with your team!
- Show your creativity.
- Showcase your skills.
- Come up with new ideas within the given time, have fun, learn and grab one of the big prizes!

Hackathon Tips

- Be open to new ideas.
- Don't be afraid to ask questions.
- Stay in constant communication with your team members.
- Be organized. Failing to plan is planning to fail.
- Manage your time well during the Hackathon.
- Work hard, show your creativity and learn a lot. Happy Hackathon!

Who can join a Hackathon?

Anyone of any age and profession who is interested in the topic of the event can join a Hackathon.

What if I have never joined a Hackathon before?

No problem! All entry-level tech talent can apply to a Hackathon.

How do you join a Hackathon?

Once you find a Hackathon that suits you, you can apply either on your own or with your team.

Do I need to know a programming language to join a Hackathon?

Hackathons are not only about coding, so even if you don't know how to code, you can showcase your other skills in a Hackathon. Hackathons also have a design and presentation side.

How long do Hackathons last?

Hackathon events usually last from 24 hours to a week. Since Hackathons are time-based, you need to plan your project well.

# **AI Hackathon with Google DeepMind**

CTICC (Cape Town International Convention Centre), 1 Lower Long Street, Cape Town, 8001

[GDG Cape Town](https://gdg.community.dev/gdg-cape-town/)

Fullday hackathon for developers, startups and researchers from South Africa to build impactful AI-enabled digital solutions that solve real-word challenges.

#### **Sep 25, 2025, 2:00 – 11:00 AM (EDT)**

194 RSVP'd

### **Key themes**

AIAI - GeminiAI - GemmaBuild with AIGoogle CloudHackathon

## About this event

Join GDG Cape Town and Google DeepMind for a first-of-its-kind AI Hackathon! This event will bring together developers, data scientists, and AI enthusiasts to collaborate, innovate, and build impactful solutions using cutting-edge Google AI technologies. The Hackathon will be a great opportunity to work alongside experienced mentors and fellow developers to expand your knowledge in AI. You’ll get to create a tangible prototype to showcase your talent and win amazing prizes while at it!

### **Important Notes**

**1\. Registration.**

1. All Hackathon participants are required to register through this platform.

2. Participants will be expected to work in groups of 3-5. If you already have a team, you can select a preferred name which you’ll get to submit during the registration process. You can still sign up as a solo developer and you’ll get a chance to select teammates on the buildup to the event


**2\. What to Build**.

The theme for the Hackathon is “AI for Impact” and participants will be required to come up with challenges under the following broad categories:

1. AgTech

2. EdTech

3. HealthTech

4. Fintech

5. GovTech


Once you’ve your idea in place, the next step is to bring the solution to life by leveraging Google’s AI tools. We expect the ideation process to take no more than 45minutes so that you have ample time to develop your prototype.

**3\. Submissions**.

1. A brief presentation covering the following areas:-



1. What problem were you working on? How did you solve the problem?

2. What did you achieve? An overview of the solution, including the technical implementation.

3. Any post-hackathon work?
2. At least one member of the team must be physically present in the Coding Hub within Innovators Hive to demo the Project to judges during the Judging Period. Presentations must include a summary of points 1-4 above. Projects with no demonstration will only be eligible to win Participation Prizes. In person demos should be no more than 2 minutes.


**4\. Judging Criteria**

1. **Wow factor** (30%) WOW-Factor is a measure of innovation you've demonstrated in your project. Does your project have a sense of magic to it?

2. **Impact** (30%) Overall value of your project to your target domain. This could be a measure of environmental impact, business impact, health impact, etc. A great project here could stand on its own as a startup or revolutionize its domain.

3. **Polish** (30%) Polish is a measure of how ready for prime-time your project is. A great project in this area will be feature complete (or close) with a pitch that would make a director want to fund your project.

4. **Presentation quality** (10%) How well you organized your idea in a deck and how clear you introduced your idea in a 3 minute pitch. An excellent presentation would be having the audience clearly understand the overarching goal of this project, the proposal details how you are solving the problem and a clear picture how this can be applicable to the problem statement.


**5\. Prizes**

1. Grand Prize (1 winner)



1. ZAR 50,000 in cash

2. $3,000 in Google Cloud Credits for use with a Cloud Billing Account
2. Runners-up



1. ZAR 40,000 in cash

2. $3,000 in Google Cloud Credits for use with a Cloud Billing Account
3. 2nd Runners-up


1. ZAR 25,000 in cash

2. $3,000 in Google Cloud Credits for use with a Cloud Billing Account

**Photography Notice**: Photography and video recordings will take place during the event. By attending the event, you agree to being photographed.
