AI Hackathons \| Otinga

[Skip to main content](https://otinga.io/services/ai-hackathons/#main-content)

AI Fluency · Organisational layer

# Turn your teams' ideas into outcomes, in days rather than quarters

Your people know where the friction is. We run the event around a real challenge your executives set and judge, in weeks not a quarter, and stay through the weeks after. If you are not ready, we say so.

Start my conversation →

![Hackathon participants at work](https://otinga.io/images/services/photos/banner-hackathons-bw.jpg)

One of three Otinga programmes, with AI Strategy and AI Dividend. The same team ran a leading bank’s 1,200-registration hackathon and impact.com’s largest AI engineering event to date.

Why this exists

## The event is rarely the hard part. The week after is.

### Great energy, no route through

Plenty of organisations run excellent innovation days. What is often missing is the path from demo to decision, so promising work goes back into a queue behind everything that was already there.

### The ideas were never the constraint

The people closest to the work know where the friction is. What they need is a route to act on it, and a reason to believe acting on it leads somewhere.

### Momentum is worth protecting

Each event that ends in a decision makes the next one easier to fill. We design for that, because your people’s willingness to lean in is one of the most valuable things you have.

What we do

## Designed, run and followed through.

### Scale the ambition

We take AI out of the central team and put it in the hands of the people who know the work. The format is built so participation is genuinely worth your teams’ time.

### Accelerate what is running

We unblock stalled initiatives in days, not quarters. Sometimes the most valuable outcome is not a new idea but an existing one finally being executed.

### Innovate in hours, not months

Hackathons built around a challenge that matters to your business, judged against criteria your executives set, with follow-through designed in from the start.

### A portfolio of outcomes, not one winner

Our events surface radical ideas, systemic improvements to how work gets done, and a host of mini-vations: small, practical changes that add up to real impact. All three are worth having.

## Formats we run.

### Internal enterprise hackathons

Your people, your challenges, your judging panel.

### Co-innovation events

Run alongside your clients or partners on a shared problem.

### Talent acquisition hackathons

Meet engineers through real work rather than another interview loop.

### Agentathons and promptathons

Shorter, sharper formats focused on AI agents and applied prompting.

Virtual, in person or hybrid. Our virtual events run in a purpose-built venue rather than a grid of video calls, which is a large part of why people stay for the whole thing.

How it runs

## Four phases, and the last one is the point.

1

### Design

We define the challenge with your executives, set success criteria and the judging rubric, plan participation, and recruit mentors and judges.

2

### Build

Applications, screening, team formation, communications and platform setup. Innovation at scale should be simple, so this runs on our platform rather than on your team’s spreadsheets.

3

### Run

Professional facilitation across the event: mentors, judging, logistics and momentum. Your people get to mentor and observe rather than administrate.

4

### Follow through

The phase most programmes skip. We support the winning teams, track progress against milestones, and report back to the executives who sponsored it.

What you leave with

## What you leave with.

- 01Working prototypes against a challenge your executives set
- 02A scored and ranked portfolio of ideas with the judging rationale attached
- 03Structured observations on how your people collaborate under real pressure
- 04A follow-through plan for what won, with owners and dates
- 05An experience your teams will talk about, which does more for your employer brand than a campaign

![Hackathon participants group photo](https://otinga.io/.netlify/images?w=1120&h=700&q=80&url=%2Fimages%2Fservices%2Fphotos%2Fgroup-bw.jpg)

## In the media.

In the media · Nedbank![Nedbank](https://otinga.io/.netlify/images?h=40&q=80&url=%2Fimages%2Flogos%2Fclients%2Fnedbank.png)

### 1,200 registrations. 50 finalists. Offers on the day.

Nedbank ran the N\*ovation Data & Analytics Masters to find and hire South Africa’s most advanced data practitioners, with Otinga as facilitation and platform partner alongside OfferZen, Zindi and Microsoft. Otinga structured the Data Engineering track and the end-to-end challenge design.

- 1,200+ registrations nationally
- Four weeks of asynchronous virtual competition
- Two tracks: Data Engineering and Machine Learning / Data Science
- 50 finalists invited to an invite-only finale at Nedbank’s Johannesburg headquarters
- R500,000+ prize pool
- Top performers received letters of intent on the day as part of a live hiring pathway

The Data Engineering track was built as a production-style pipeline challenge that changed under the competitors, testing maintainability, scalability and efficiency as requirements shifted. That is not a puzzle. That is the job. A CV cannot show you how someone handles a moving brief.

[Read the full story →](https://it-online.co.za/2026/06/24/nedbank-uncovers-data-talent-through-national-analytics-challenge/) As featured in IT Online

In the media · impact.com![impact.com](https://otinga.io/.netlify/images?h=40&q=80&url=%2Fimages%2Flogos%2Fclients%2Fimpact-com.png)

### 250 engineers. One day. Their largest AI engineering event ever.

impact.com brought its global engineering organisation to Cape Town for the TTP Tech Hackathon as part of its Developer Summit. Otinga was facilitation and platform partner, translating strategic objectives into challenge framing, team workflows and execution pathways.

- 250+ engineers, product managers and technical leaders in one room
- One-day build sprint, 23 April 2026, Cape Town
- Run against real product challenges, not sandbox exercises
- Built on the tooling teams actually use, including Cursor and Gemini
- The largest AI-focused engineering event impact.com has held

> Working with Otinga allowed us to structure that process in a way that moved teams from ideas to execution quickly, while still maintaining a high bar for impact. The result is not just prototypes, but a clearer path to how AI can accelerate productivity across our engineering organisation.

Most AI adoption is demos and slides. If your AI story does not change what your engineers ship at scale, it is theatre. The measure is output, not enthusiasm.

[Read the full story →](https://ai-impact.co.za/otinga-io-leads-landmark-ai-hackathon-with-impact-com-bringing-250-global-engineers-to-cape-town/) As featured in AI Impact

## Who it is for.

### Heads of Innovation, Data and AI

### Executive sponsors who want visible proof the organisation can move

### Talent leaders in a market where everyone is approached weekly

### Business unit leaders with a problem that has been stuck for a while

FAQs

## Common questions.

How is this different from the hackathon we already ran internally?

Follow-through, and executives set the challenge and criteria first.

Virtual, in person, or hybrid, which should we run?

Virtual reaches more people; in person suits teams who rarely meet. We usually recommend hybrid.

How much of our people's time does this actually take?

The event, plus a few hours’ prep for mentors and judges.

What does this cost?

No rate card, price depends on format and scale. The scoping call ends with a defined shape and cost.

What happens to the ideas, or candidates, that do not win?

They stay yours, scored and ranked.

What if our executives cannot agree on the challenge or criteria in advance?

The most common reason a hackathon slips, and what Phase 1 solves.

Both results you show are hiring outcomes. Is this actually about building AI capability?

Yes: hiring results carry a named citation, but both use the same rubric and Phase 4.

## Where this leads.

To turn what came out of the event into costed business cases with owners.\\
Explore AI Dividend →](https://otinga.io/services/ai-dividend/)

SAVE THE DATE · 22 OCTOBER 2026


# Connecting the Brightest Minds at the KZN AI Summit 2026

Join industry leaders, innovators, academics, heads of state and entrepreneurs in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal as we explore the future of artificial intelligence, drive collaboration and unlock new opportunities across the SADC tech ecosystem.


[Register Now](https://qkt.io/OMXYJS) [Explore the Summit](https://kznaisummit.co.za/about-event.html)

Summit Countdown

12Days

15Hours

42Mins

51Secs

Durban ICC, KwaZulu-Natal

08:00 SAST, 22 October 2026

Who You'll Meet

## A Room Built for Every Corner of the AI Ecosystem

Funders & Venture CapitalistsGovernment Officials & MunicipalitiesPrivate Sector CEOs & COOsAcademia & CollegesResearch OrganisationsNGOs & Civil SocietyEntrepreneurs & AI EnthusiastsInnovation Managers

![KZN AI Summit 2026 - Save the Date, 22 October 2026, Durban ICC](https://kznaisummit.co.za/images/revolution/save-the-date.jpg)

2030

KZN's target as SA's AI hub

Join the Revolution

## Dive Into Innovation and Connect with Tech Leaders

KZN AI Summit is the first premier AI event for tech enthusiasts and professionals eager to explore the latest in AI advancements. Embrace the future at the KZN AI Summit and SADC AI Hackathon 2026.

South Africa is experiencing a transformative wave of investment in AI infrastructure, and KwaZulu-Natal is positioning itself as the country's third AI hub. This is where that future gets decided.

21+

Expert speakers

500+

Delegates expected

On the Agenda

## Key Topics at KZN AI Summit 2026

Seven tracks shaping the conversation, from policy and governance to the next decade of artificial intelligence.

01

### AI Policy & Governance

- Ethical AI Frameworks – Balancing innovation & accountability.
- Regulating AI in SA – Policies for inclusive, secure adoption.
- Public Sector AI Standards – Ensuring transparency & fairness.

02

### SADC States & AI Leadership

- National AI Strategy – Aligning provincial, national & SADC AI goals.
- Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) – Collaborative AI funding & projects.
- AI for Service Delivery – Enhancing healthcare, education & utilities.

03

### Smart Cities & Municipal AI

- IoT & AI-Driven Infrastructure – Traffic, energy & waste management.
- Engagement Tech – Web3, AI chatbots & data-driven decision-making.
- Case Studies – Global smart city lessons for KZN.

04

### Academic Institutions' AI Revolution

- Curriculum Transformation – Integrating AI across disciplines.
- Research & Innovation Hubs – Cutting-edge AI projects in KZN universities.
- Industry-Academia Collaboration – Bridging theory and real-world applications.
- AI Skills Development – Preparing graduates for the AI-driven job market.
- Emerging Technologies Lab – Showcasing student-led AI innovations.

05

### AI for Economic Sectors

- Agriculture – Precision farming, drone monitoring & AI supply chains.
- Retail – Personalised shopping, inventory and delivery AI tech.
- Financial Services – Fraud detection, robo-advisors & blockchain AI.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know before you register.

When and where is the KZN AI Summit 2026?

The summit takes place on 22 October 2026 at the Durban International Convention Centre (ICC), Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Doors open at 08:00 SAST.

How do I get tickets?

Tickets are sold through Quicket. Click any Register Now or Get Tickets button on this site and you will be taken straight to our official Quicket page to complete your booking.

Can my company sponsor or exhibit?

Yes. We offer Silver, Gold and Platinum sponsorship packages plus Basic, Standard and Premium exhibition stands. Visit the Sponsorships page for full pricing and benefits, or contact us directly.

Who should attend?

The summit is built for government officials, funders and venture capitalists, private sector leaders, academia and researchers, NGOs, entrepreneurs and anyone serious about AI's impact on South Africa and the SADC region.

Is there an option to speak at the summit?

We review speaker applications on an ongoing basis. Head to the Speakers page and use the Apply to Speak button, or email us directly with your topic and background.

How can I get updates before the event?

Sign up for our newsletter in the footer of any page, or follow KZN AI Summit on Facebook for speaker announcements, agenda updates and ticket news.

pageTitle: #AyobaHack: Ayoba Virtual Hackathon in South Africa - Devpost
title: #AyobaHack
description: Ayoba is a messaging platform aimed at meeting the needs of African consumers and businesses. This hackathon will encourage developers to create services through micro-apps and will feature access to a developer sandbox environment as well as coaching support.
eligibility: Open to South African developers.
prizes: ZAR150,000 in prizes, with R100,000 for 1st place, R30,000 for 2nd place, R20,000 for 3rd place, and prizes for the Top 5 teams.
teamRequirements: Teams must present a project profile, a PowerPoint presentation of up to 10 slides, a demo video, supporting project assets, and last Git commit screenshots.
rawMarkdown:
# \#AyobaHack ### Ayoba Virtual Hackathon in South Africa **This hackathon has ended** [Find more hackathons](https://devpost.com/hackathons) [View the winners](https://ayobahack.devpost.com/project-gallery) [View full rules](https://ayobahack.devpost.com/rules) [View schedule](https://ayobahack.devpost.com/details/dates) **Apr 3 – 6, 2020** | | | | --- | --- | | Online | Public | | [**ZAR150,000** in prizes](https://ayobahack.devpost.com/#prizes) | **142**
participants | [Geek Ulcha / Ayoba](https://devpost.com/hackathons?organization=Geek+Ulcha+%2F+Ayoba) [Fintech](https://devpost.com/hackathons?themes%5B%5D=Fintech) [Voice skills](https://devpost.com/hackathons?themes%5B%5D=Voice+skills) [Social Good](https://devpost.com/hackathons?themes%5B%5D=Social+Good) YouTube Tap to unmute Video unavailable [Visit YouTube to search for more videos](https://www.youtube.com/) Video unavailable This video is unavailable Ayoba is a messaging platform, with support to channels, payments, bots and micro apps/service agents. It is localised for African and Middle East consumer needs. Ayoba, together with the UCTGSB Solution Space and Geekulcha, will be hosting a virtual hackathon on 03 - 06 April for South African developers. The event aims to introduce the opening of Ayoba as a platform for developers and the MicroApp to 3rd parties. Top 5 teams from the virtual Hackathon will then compete for a Top spot for the grand prizes at a physical 1-day Hackathon venue or a guided virtual participation platform. Developers will have an opportunity to get creative and launch services through micro-apps. Over two days, developers and start-ups will be given preview access to a developer sandbox environment. The teams will also have access to coaches providing tech, UI/UX and business support. _**The challenge:**_ _Make creative use of the Ayoba platform to build services and solutions that meet the daily needs of African consumers and businesses._ After the four days, teams will submit their work to a panel of experts. The teams that develop the winning solutions will receive complimentary co-working space at the Ayoba offices, technical, marketing & development support as well as R150k in prize money for the hackathon’s Top 3 teams. The top 3 ideas will be considered for the UCTGSB Solution Space E-Track Programme in partnership with the MTN Group. ### Eligibility In order to receive the prize(s), you will need to agree to the Terms and Conditions that will be sent to you via email. ### Requirements - Project profile as guided on ayobahack.devpost.com - PowerPoint presentation of no more than 10 slides (including a slide with members short bios, problem + solution, Business Model Canvas,  screenshots of project, etc.) - Demo video of the project - Supporting assets of project - Last Git commit screenshots (up to 10 on Git platform of choice) ### Hackathon Sponsors ### Prizes ZAR150,000 in prizes ###### 1st Place 1 winner R100 000.00 ###### 2nd Place 1 winner R30000 ###### 3rd Place 1 winner R20000 ###### Made it Top 5 5 winners Top 5 teams that made it to the finale. ===== BATTLE OF THE 5 TEAMS ===== The Top 3 teams that develop the winning solutions will receive complimentary co-working space at the Ayoba offices, technical, marketing & development support as well as R150k (slip into 3 ) in prize money for the hackathon’s Top 3 teams. ### Devpost Achievements Submitting to this hackathon could earn you: ### Judges ![Lebogang Madise](https://d112y698adiu2z.cloudfront.net/photos/production/judge_photos/001/009/271/datas/large.png) **Lebogang Madise** _Future Ready Skills Lead (Middle East & Africa), Microsoft_ ![ Zachariah George ](https://d112y698adiu2z.cloudfront.net/photos/production/judge_photos/001/007/257/datas/large.png) **Zachariah George** _Chief Investment Officer @Startupbootcamp Africa_ ![Muzi Ntombela](https://d112y698adiu2z.cloudfront.net/photos/production/judge_photos/001/019/656/datas/large.png) **Muzi Ntombela** _CIO, Centre for Public Service Innovation_ ![David Gilarranz](https://d112y698adiu2z.cloudfront.net/photos/production/judge_photos/001/007/260/datas/large.png) **David Gilarranz** _Group CEO Digital, MTN Group_ ![ Thomas Schulze ](https://d112y698adiu2z.cloudfront.net/photos/production/judge_photos/001/007/262/datas/large.png) **Thomas Schulze** _Head of Product, Ayoba_ ![Yusuf Yabo](https://d112y698adiu2z.cloudfront.net/photos/production/judge_photos/001/087/554/datas/large.png) **Shiela Yabo** _Manager, UCT GSB Solution Space_ ### Judging Criteria - **1\. Innovation and Novelty** How unique is the solution? How does it improve or leverage existing systems to create larger social or business impact? How feasible is the solution? - **2\. Business Model** Is the concept desirable? Does it look like it will have customers and market thereof. Is there a potentially viable business model? Each team is required to outline these aspects: Customer Segment, Value Proposition, Revenue Streams and Key Activities. - **3\. The Use of Ayoba Platform** How best did the team make use of the Ayoba APIs to build a solution? Does it integrate well with current Ayoba functionality? Did the team bring a wow factor or suggested a feature? Did the team use any additional web frameworks? Quality of code? - **4\. User Experience** How complex is the solution? Is the focal feature minimally functional? Does it have ease of use/navigation to find needs? - **5\. Local Relevance and Impact** Does the idea solve locally relevant issues? Does it do so in an impactful way? Questions? ### Frequently Asked Questions - Software Engineering Conferences in South Africa

How can I get an invitation letter for Software Engineering conferences in South Africa?

In order to receive a visa invitation letter for the Software Engineering South Africa conference, you must first register for the event and pay the fees through official registration form. And then send request to conference organizer via email for 'Visa Support / Invitation Letter'. Please include full name, passport number and place of issue, organisation (speaker/participant), position (speakers/participants) and travel dates.

What are the Software Engineering conferences in South Africa in 2026–2027?

Software Engineering conferences in South Africa in 2026–2027 are a gathering of professionals, industry experts, researchers, and scholars who discuss current challenges and solutions in Software Engineering. At these global events, you can get networking opportunities, paper presentation, poster presentation, and other chances to glorify your future work or career.

Why attend a Software Engineering conference in South Africa?

Attending a Software Engineering conference in South Africa means you are connecting directly with national and international leaders, learning new skills, meeting like-minded people, and showcasing your work at global platforms. It gives you tie-ups, exposure to new research and ways in which relevant Software Engineering issues are dealt with in the academic/industry/regulatory culture of South Africa.

How can I register for an upcoming Software Engineering conference in South Africa?

Visit the official conference website and find the Registration page. Select your participation type (in-person, virtual, or hybrid), fill in your personal and professional details, and pay the registration fee if required. After registering, you’ll receive confirmation and access instructions. Some Software Engineering conferences in South Africa also allow early-bird registration with discounted fees.

Are online or hybrid Software Engineering conferences available in South Africa?

Yes — many Software Engineering events in several countries now feature virtual and hybrid options. The conferences offer a comprehensive hybrid participation option, providing livestream access (to return and watch replays on demand) and virtual networking tools in addition to the regular attendance at a physical event, mostly catering to international participants with travel difficulty. Dress code details are available on the official site for each event.

Can I submit research papers to Software Engineering conferences in South Africa?

Yes most academic and professional Software Engineering conferences in South Africa have a Call for Papers (CFP) inviting submissions. You can submit an abstract or full paper through the conference’s online submission portal before the deadline. Submissions go through peer review, and accepted papers are presented as talks or posters and often included in published proceedings.

<hackathon-10th-anniversary>

2 & 3 June 2026 \| Sandton Convention Centre

In a hyper-connected digital universe, cybersecurity isn’t optional, it’s mission critical. As the ITWeb Security Summit Hackathon marks its 10-year milestone, we rally the next generation of innovators under one banner: Hackers Assemble!

This year’s challenge? Unleash the power of AI to fortify cyber resilience. Design intelligent, adaptive solutions that can predict, detect and neutralise threats in real time. From AI-driven threat detection to automated response and advanced security analytics, the mission is clear; outpace adversaries and engineer the future of defence.

Created by ITWeb in partnership with Geekulcha, the hackathon was born to tackle the industry’s critical cybersecurity skills gap. A decade later, it remains a launchpad for young developers, techpreneurs and security enthusiasts to horn their skills, collaborate with seasoned mentors, and build real-world cyber defence strategies.

In 2026, bright local talent will once again converge at the Sandton Convention Centre, alongside the ITWeb Security Summit 2026, to code, collaborate and innovate in an electric atmosphere charged with curiosity and purpose.

For ten years, this hackathon has empowered builders of the digital frontier.

Now it’s your turn.

Hackers Assemble.

Let’s defend the digital world and build what comes next.


Hackathon Timeline

10 February 2026

Registration will officially open for the hackathon as an open call and closes on 10 April 2026.

11 April 2026

The IDEATHON will take place virtually.

30 April 2026

Submission will close for the post IDEATHON work in consideration for participation for the Assembly hackathon.

10 May 2026

Teams are informed that they will participate onto the hackathon through an automated Sonke process.

22-23 May 2026

With unlimited number of participants, the Assembly Hackathon will take place virtual and will produce the Top Teams.

27 May 2026

Pre-hackathon finale briefing to prepare the final teams for participation, hosted virtually.

2-3 June 2026

Top 10 Secure Innovation and Top CTF Challenge teams battle it out physically at the Sandton Convention Centre.

3 June 2026

Top 3 teams and CTF Challenge winners are announced on the stage at the ITWeb Security Summit 2026.

FOR THE PARTICIPANTS

**ITWeb** in partnership with [Geekulcha](https://www.geekulcha.dev/), invites you to step onto the front lines of the digital battlefield, a world of deception, misdirection, and relentless cyber threats, where only the sharpest minds stand between chaos and control. This is the world of cybersecurity, zero trust, and digital defence, and in 2026, we’re calling on the heroes to rise.

If you have IT or cybersecurity skills and you’re ready to test your limits, or level up fast, this is your arena. Learn directly from industry-leading professionals, go head-to-head with top talent from across the ecosystem, and compete for cash prizes, career-launching opportunities, and serious bragging rights.

The journey kicks off with the Ideathon, the official starting point of #SS26Hack. This high-energy phase is all about training, ideation, and team selection, setting you up for success. You’ll gain insider insight into today’s cyber threat landscape, explore real-world challenges, and refine your ideas under the guidance of expert mentors before moving into the main hackathon.

Whether you’re here to sharpen your skills, prove your expertise, or help defend the digital future, this is where it begins.

Suit up. Skill up. Hackers Assemble.

You'll team up in groups and apply for challenges or submit ideas of what you can build or showcase, and where the top entries will be taken through to the main event, held alongside ITWeb's 21st Security Summit, the definitive event for information security professionals.

[Register Now](https://www.itweb.co.za/event/itweb-security-summit-2026/hackathon/registration)

The IDEATHON

To prepare participants for the Hackathon, **this year, a virtual IDEATHON will be held on 11th April** for training and idea generation. A panel of industry leaders will run training sessions for the participants to acquire concepts and guidance in development of their **#SS26Hack** projects. Teams will then be selected to participate at the **virtual Assembly Hackathon from 22-23 May**. After this, the top teams will be chosen, whom will attend the final **Live Hackathon** at the **ITWeb Security Summit** in Sandton.

rawMarkdown:
[Skip to content](https://hack4dev.org/dshp-organisers-call/#content "Skip to content")

**Are you interested in hosting a data science hackathon in your local region?**

Hack4dev invites interested groups to apply to Stage 1 of its Data Science Hackathon Cascade Programme (DSH-CP). Selected teams will

- a) receive training on how to run a hackathon through an **Organisers Hackathon**, and
- b) be supported to host a hackathon at your home institute.

The **Organisers Hackathon** for organisers will take place in Cape Town, South Africa, in **May 2026**. Continue reading to learn more about the call.

* * *

# 1\. Introduction

**After the success of the 2024–2025 DSH-CP, Hack4dev is pleased to announce the launch of its second cycle, running in 2025–2026.** The first cycle brought together more than 150 participants across 12 countries in 13 regional hackathons worldwide. Building on this momentum, the upcoming cycle aims to grow even further, with an expanded network of coordinated hackathons across the globe.

The DSHP is structured in two stages. For full details, please visit ( [link](https://hack4dev.org/ds-hackathon/)), but in brief:

- **Stage 1: Organisers Hackathon (OH)** A four-day event in which regional organisers gain first-hand experience in both the logistical and technical aspects of running a data science hackathon.
- **Stage 2: Regional Hackathons (RH)** Organisers then host hackathons at their own institutions, all focused on the same challenge. This creates opportunities for global participation and allows results to be compared across regions.

# 2\. Key Dates

**For Organisers Hackathon (OH):**

- **Applications Open:** 1 Oct – 10 Nov 2025 (extended)
- **Results Announcement:** 17 Dec 2025
- **Organisers Hackathon Event:** May 2026

**For Regional Hackathons (RH):**

- **Regional Organisers issue Call for Hackathon Participants Across All Regions:** June 2026
- Regional Hackathons Hosting Period: August – October 2026 (exact timing to be determined)

* * *

# 3\. This Call is for Stage 1: Organisers

This call specifically invites applications for the **Organisers Hackathon (OH)**.

Selected organisers will then be supported by Hack4dev to implement Regional Hackathons in their own institutions during Stage 2 of the programme.

![](https://hack4dev.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/DSC03083-2-scaled.jpg)

# 4\. Who should apply

We are looking for dynamic teams with a mix of data science knowledge and event organisation skills. Applicants should have the motivation and capacity to dedicate time and energy to running a hackathon. We welcome applications from post-graduate students and others with the skills and commitment to lead successfully.

# 5\. What is required to apply?

- A dedicated team of organisers, with a designated team leader responsible for the application.
- Availability of a suitable venue to host the Regional Hackathon.

# 6\. Eligibility

#### **_Applicants must meet the following:_**

- **Team Lead**
  - **Skill Set:** The team lead must have strong knowledge in both data science and event organisation.
  - **Commitment:** Must take a leading role in executing the regional hackathon, including but not limited to coordination, communication, and timely delivery of all activities.
- Teams must consist of 3–5 **committed** members. As a group, they should demonstrate a mix of experience in:

  - **Event organisation** (including communication, logistics, etc.), and
  - **Data science** (either through work or research experience)
- **Local Recruitment Capacity:** Teams should be able to recruit participants from their own and nearby institutions, ensuring that all participants at least have strong Python skills. Further details about the Regional Hackathon eligibility will be shared at a later stage.
- **Organisers Hackathon Participation:** At least one member (preferably the team leader) from each accepted team is required to attend the Hack4dev Organisers Hackathon event in person, hosted in **Cape Town, South Africa**, with the remaining team members participating online.
- **Hackathon Execution**: All teams must commit to organising Regional Hackathons at their institutions within the suggested time frame of August – October 2026
- **Code of Conduct:** Adherence to the [HACKATHON CODE OF CONDUCT](https://hack4dev.org/hackathon-code-of-conduct/) is mandatory, ensuring a respectful, inclusive, and productive environment for all participants.
- **Venue:** Teams must secure a suitable venue at their own institution to host the hackathon. The venue should provide the essential requirements for a smooth event, including a reliable electricity supply with enough sockets, a stable and reasonably fast internet connection (minimum of 4 Mbps), adequate seating and workspace for all participants, and a quiet, safe environment that supports focused collaboration. The venue must have the capacity to accommodate at least 25 participants.
- **Participant Equipment:** For Regional Hackathons, participants are expected to bring their own laptops to access the cloud computing infrastructure, especially in venues not equipped with computers.
- **Global Participation:** The call is open to teams worldwide. Regardless of your location, we encourage you to apply if you have the skills and the drive.
- **Gender Balance:** In cases of tied scores within one standard deviation, and within the same country, preference will be given to the application that helps improve overall gender balance among team leads, provided that all teams meet the minimum eligibility and quality requirements.

#### **Limitations and Funding:**

- **Regional Hackathon Costs**: Regional hackathons are designed to be easy to implement and low-cost, enabling them to reach a broader community. Therefore, no accommodation or transport fees will be encouraged. All participants should be able to commute daily to and from the regional hackathon venue.
- **Participant Cap for Regional Hackathons:** Teams should aim for a minimum of 25 participants per hackathon.
- **Financial Support:** Teams are encouraged to find local funding to organise the Regional Hackathon (approximately 60,000 ZAR) and cover travel and participation in the Organisers’ Hackathon.

Hack4dev has limited funding available and will aim to raise additional funds. Depending on the outcome, selected teams may receive either a partial grant of up to 15,000 ZAR or a full grant covering both travel to the Organisers Hackathon and Regional Hackathon expenses.
- Hackathon organiser roles are voluntary. Applicants should note that there is no compensation or stipend provided for organising a hackathon.

# 7\. Selection Framework

|     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selection Criterion | Corresponding Questions in the Application Form | Scoring Guideline |
| Team Composition and Experience | Questions regarding the team lead and the team (2k, 4a-4e) | 12 |
| Motivation and Impact | Questions regarding the Team’s motivation and impact (5a-5c) | 6 |
| Implementation Plan | Questions regarding communication and venue (3d-3f) | 6 |
| Budget and Financial Summary | Projected Budget (6c) | 2 |

# 8\. Support and Resources for Selected Teams

#### Selected Teams Will Receive:

- **Capacity Building:** Opportunities to strengthen and expand data science skills within their own region.
- **Training and Guidance:** Ongoing support from the Hack4dev team on both operational aspects and the hackathon challenge, provided before, during, and after the Organisers Hackathon to ensure the successful delivery of each Regional Hackathon.
- **Practical Resources:** Access to explanatory notebooks and a real-world research project, designed in collaboration with field experts, which will serve as the challenge for the next round of Regional Hackathons.
- **Cloud Computing Support:** Access to high-performance computational resources to enable both organisers and Regional Hackathon participants to develop, test, and run their solutions effectively.
- **Research Contribution:** Organisers who actively work on the real-world challenge and submit solutions during the Organisers Hackathon as part of a team will be considered for co-authorship in the upcoming Hackathon Data Science Paper.
- **Hack4dev Regional Nodes:** Outstanding teams from the Regional Hackathons may be invited to form official Hack4dev Regional Nodes. These nodes will serve as local hubs to continue developing skills, advancing innovations, and supporting future hackathon activities in their regions.
- **Recognition and Awards:** Entry into a prize for the best organising team across all Regional Hackathons, celebrating excellence in organisation and impact.

[Applications Closed](https://forms.gle/8PfnAZ8JRTDmqVgW9)

## Building Community Hackathon Series

### Creating innovative digital solutions to key social, environmental, health, and economic challenges facing South Africans today.

[Find Out More](https://hackon.co.za/building-community-hackathon-series/)

![](https://hackon.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/200px-U.S._Department_of_State_official_seal.svg_-1.png)

##### WHAT IS A HACKATHON?

# **An event, typically lasting several days, in which a large number of people meet to engage in collaborative computer programming.**

##### about us

The Silicon Cape Initiative is partnering with the U.S. Embassy and Consulates in South Africa to host four hackathons — two in Cape Town and two in Johannesburg. The hackathons focus on a real-world challenge that South Africans face today, like preventing gender-based violence, unemployment, or lack of access to economic opportunities.

We are looking for emerging software developers, IT professionals and trainers, civil society organisations, academics and professionals in relevant fields of chosen topics to join us.

We have R160 000 up for grabs to winning teams and also spot prizes during the duration of hackathons.

You do not want to miss out!

Participating in the hackathon will give you the opportunity to meet new people, learn more about design thinking, service design and come with an innovative and socially impactful service or product.

![](https://hackon.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Silicon-Cape-Initiative-Logo-Long.png)

![](https://hackon.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/200px-U.S._Department_of_State_official_seal.svg_-1.png)

## **Who is**  The Silicon Cape Initiative?

Silicon Cape is an NPO and an ecosystem enabler for tech-enabled startups in the boarder Cape Region of South Africa. We work to connect stakeholders, curate ecosystem data, amplify the stories coming out of the ecosystem and advocate on behalf of stakeholders through its membership programme.

[www.siliconcape.com](http://www.siliconcape.com/)

## **Who is**  the U.S. Embassy?

The United States Diplomatic Mission to South Africa represents the government of the United States in South Africa. In addition to the Embassy in Pretoria it includes Consulates in Cape Town, Johannesburg, and Durban. The Public Affairs Section of the Embassy and its Consulates provides occasional funding opportunities for projects and activities that support our Public Diplomacy work in South Africa.

See [https://za.usembassy.gov/](https://za.usembassy.gov/) for more about the work of the U.S. Embassy.

### Project Background

Hackathons for South Africa: Digital Solutions for Real World

Challenges

In 2019, the U.S. Embassy’s Public Affairs Section selected The Silicon Cape Initiative to run a series of hackathons in South Africa to build technical, problem-solving, creative thinking, and collaborative skills among emerging software developers to strengthen their employability and help drive economic growth. At the same time, the hackathons are intended to create innovative digital solutions to key social, environmental, health, and economic challenges as well as strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and South Africa through exchanges of information, experiences, and expertise.

The first hackathon was held in November 2019 in Cape Town and focused on solutions to prevent gender-based violence. COVID required that Silicon Cape pivot to a virtual hackathon model, and so the second hackathon was held virtually in October 2020 in coordination with the U.S. Consulate in Johannesburg and the Rosa Parks Library. Participants came up with innovative solutions to address community safety challenges.

Building on the success of the virtual hackathon model, the third hackathon, scheduled for June 2021, will also be virtual and will focus on accelerating economic growth in township-based small businesses. The fourth and final hackathon is targeted for the end of 2021.

Will Stevens, Acting Consul General at the U.S. Consulate in Cape Town says: “As the cradle of the fourth industrial revolution, the United States understands the tremendous impact that crowd-sourcing and digital creativity can have in solving the tough problems in our societies. That is why we are so proud to sponsor Silicon Cape’s upcoming series of Hackathons in South Africa. We believe that these programmes will bring top coders, young entrepreneurs and civic activists together to help address tough issues in South African Society.”

“We are incredibly proud to have been selected and this honour further proves that the Cape is indeed considered a hub for innovation. We look forward to seeing the solutions that emerge from the hackathons and how they can benefit South Africans,” adds Silicon Cape Chairperson, Dr Sumarie Roodt.
